en.title: New Maldives High Commissioner to Malaysia presents credentials
en.description: 20 June 2014: The new High Commissioner of the Republic of Maldives to Malaysia His Excellency Mr. Mohamed Fayaz has presented his Letter of Credence to the King of Malaysia the Yang di Pertuan Agong XIV, His Majesty Al Mu'tasimu Billahi Muhibbuddin Tuanku Alhaj Abdul Halim Mu'adzam Shah Ibni…
en.body:
20 June 2014: The new High Commissioner of the Republic of Maldives to Malaysia His Excellency Mr. Mohamed Fayaz has presented his Letter of Credence to the King of Malaysia the Yang di Pertuan Agong XIV, His Majesty Al Mu'tasimu Billahi Muhibbuddin Tuanku Alhaj Abdul Halim Mu'adzam Shah Ibni Almarhum Sultan Badlishah today.

During the ceremony held at the National Palace, Istana Negara, the High Commissioner conveyed the goodwill and greetings of His Excellency President Yameen Abdul GAyoom and the people of Maldives to His Majesty the King, the Government and the people of Malaysia. Commending the Malaysian leadership the High Commissioner stated that the country's leaders have "transformed the country to a prosperous urban and industrialised nation that serves as examples to its Asian neighbours and to the rest of the world. [And] The rapid developmental progress attained by Malaysia serves as testimony to the vision of its Government and the fortitude of its people."

Continuing his remarks the High Commissioner noted that over the last few years Malaysia has become a home-away-from-home for a large number of Maldivians and that in this regard, the Government was working towards easing the existing bilateral visa regime. To this effect, the High Commissioner expressed his confidence in receiving the kind support of His Majesty the King and extended an invitation to the Yang d-Pertuan to visit the Maldives at a convenient time.

In his remarks His Majesty the King highlighted that Malaysia and the Maldives have been enjoying warm and close bilateral relations since its establishment in 1968 and that indeed "the two countries have undertaken concerted efforts towards expanding the scope and dimension of bilateral relations".

"Malaysia remains firmly committed in efforts to strengthen the close bilateral ties with Maldives [and] we see plenty of potential and scope abound for both countries to expand relations in the context of joint aspirations to achieve rapid social and economic development", said His Majesty.

Today's ceremony was attended by the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Malaysia His Excellency Dato' Sri Anifah Haj Aman.

The Minister at the High Commission Ms. Liusha Zahir and Counsellor Mr. Hassan Khalid also accompanied the High Commissioner today's ceremony.

ENDS.

en.title: New South Korean Ambassador presents Credentials to the President
en.description: 19 June 2014, Male'; The new South Korean Ambassador accredited to the Maldives, H. ‎E. Chang Won-sam, ‎presented his letter of credence to President Abdulla ‎Yameen Abdul Gayoom, this morning.‎
en.body:
19 June 2014, Male'; The new South Korean Ambassador accredited to the Maldives, H. ‎E. Chang Won-sam, ‎presented his letter of credence to President Abdulla ‎Yameen Abdul Gayoom, this morning.‎

At the ceremony held at the President's Office to present the ‎credentials, President Yameen congratulated the Ambassador on the ‎commencement of his term. ‎

Meeting the new Ambassador afterwards, the President highlighted ‎the Maldives' commitment to strengthening the long-standing bilateral ties ‎between the Maldives and South Korea, and stated that future economic ‎cooperation is key to enhancing relations. In this regard, President Yameen ‎emphasized the importance of increasing Korean corporate investments in ‎the Maldives.‎

Ambassador Chang conveyed to President Yameen the good wishes ‎of South Korean President Park Geun-hye and stated that South Korea ‎cherishes and values its close relationship with the Maldives. The ‎Ambassador reiterated South Korea's commitment to supporting the ‎economic development of the Maldives.‎

The President and the Ambassador also explored opportunities ‎for ‎increasing cooperation between the Maldives and South Korea on issues of ‎trade, tourism and training. ‎

The meeting was attended by the Minister at the President's Office, ‎Hon. Mohamed Hussain Shareef, Foreign Secretary Dr. Ali Naseer ‎Mohamed, and the First Secretary of the Embassy of South Korea, Mr. ‎Jeong Dongik.‎

ENDS.

en.title: "Islamic principles and values of justice and equality of all humans is well in line with modern democratic values" says Minister Dunya Maumoon
en.description: 18 June 2014, Jeddah; "Islamic principles and values of justice and equality of all humans, and the right of citizens in having a say and a stake in their governments is well in line with modern democratic values" says Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ms Dunya Maumoon. Speaking at the 41st session of…
en.body:
18 June 2014, Jeddah; "Islamic principles and values of justice and equality of all humans, and the right of citizens in having a say and a stake in their governments is well in line with modern democratic values" says Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ms Dunya Maumoon. Speaking at the 41st session of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), the Minister urged the OIC to be united in its support for democratic change around the world and in Islamic societies. She cited Maldives as an example of a modern democratic country that adhered to Islamic values. The Foreign Minister said that the Maldives was an emerging democracy that is striving to advance its democratic institutions, as well as cherish the values of Islam.

On the issue of violence against women and girls, the Foreign Minister noted that "Just a month back we heard the news of the nearly 200 kidnapped girls by Boko Haram in Nigeria in shock and disbelief.These girls were punished for seeking to learn and to educate themselves.

The Minister spoke of the deep impact Islam had on the rights of women. "The pre-Quranic times were testing times for women…Islam liberated women", she argued, citing that Islam offered women explicit rights to inheritance, independent property rights, access to divorce and the right to testify in a court of law. Islam, she said, also prohibited violence against women and girls. She urged the OIC, as the prime organisation for the cultivation and projection of true Islamic values around the globe, to work to protect, safeguard and guarantee the rights of Muslim women the world over.

Minister Dunya noted "Islam emphasises the equal rights and responsibilities of men and women"

The Minister also urged the Council of Foreign Ministers to make a thorough self-assessment to examine why Islam is increasingly being associated with intolerance, terrorism, violence and backwardness. The chaos and the upheaval the Islamic world is witnessing, she argued, are caused by the inability to exercise true Islamic ideals. While condemning Islamophobia she noted that it is easy for us to blame the West and Western media.She noted that we as Muslim societies need to make a self-assessment why Islam was being tarnished by an image linked to terrorism. Foreign Minister Dunya noted the need to change the association of Islam with intolerance, terrorism, violence and backwardness.

Finishing her address the Minister noted that "Muslims were once the pioneers of science and technology. Today, we have to accept the reality that Muslim societies are on the brink of falling into an abyss for creativity. It is beyond imagination, or within the realm of belief, to think that we can overcome these dark times? Let us recommit ourselves to work together to overcome our challenges. United and strong we can once again become the standard bearers of tolerance and innovation".

ENDS.

en.title: Foreign Minister Dunya departs to Jeddah for the OIC Foreign Ministers Meeting

en.body:
15 June 2014, Male':Foreign Minister Dunya Maumoon has departed for Jeddah this evening for the Foreign Ministers' meeting of the Organization of the Islamic Cooperation (OIC).

Minister Dunya is accompanied by His Excellency Mr. Abdullah Hameed, Ambassador-at-large at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Ms. Mariyam Midhfa Naeem, Assistant Director at the Ministry.

The 41st Session of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the OIC would be held in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. The Foreign Ministers of the fifty-seven member organization is expected to discuss ways in addressing some of the major challenges facing the Islamic Ummah.

The OIC was established in September 1969. The Maldives joined the organisation in 1976.

ENDS

12 ޖުަލައި 2014؛ ފަލަސްތީނުގައި ހިނގަމުންދާ ލޭއޮހޮރުވުމަށް ނިމުމެއްނައިސް ކުރިއަށްދިއުމަކީ ހިތްތަކަށް ކެތްކުރެވޭނެވަރުގެ ކަމެއްނޫން ކަމަށާއި އެކަމަށް ވަގުތުން ހައްލު ހޯދުމަކީ ބައިނަލްއަގްވާމީ މުޖުތަމައުގެ ވަރަށް މުޙިއްމު މަސްއޫލިއްޔަތެއްކަމަށް މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް ދުންޔާ މައުމޫން މިއަދު ވިދާޅުވެއްޖެއެވެ.

ގާޒާއަށް އިޒްރޭލުން ގެންދާ ޢުދުވާނީ ހަމަލާގައި ކުށެއްނެތް އެތަކެއް ކުޑަކުދިންނާއި އަންހެނުންނާއި ފިރިހެނުން މަރުވަމުންދާއިރު އެމީހުން ސަލާމަތްކުރުމަށް ދުނިޔޭގެ ޤައުމުތަކުން އެކަށީގެންވާ މަސައްކަތަކެއް ނުކުރެވޭތީ އެކަމަށް ރާއްޖެއިން ހިތާމަކުރާކަމަށް މިނިސްޓަރ ދުންޔާ ވިދާޅުވިއެވެ. އަދި ގާޒާގައި ހިނގާ ހަމަނުޖެހުމަކީ ބައިނަލްއަގްވާމީ ސަލާމަތަށް ހުރި ނުރައްކަލެއްކަމަށާއި އެކަމަށް އދ. ގެ ސަލާމަތީ މަޖިލީހުން ފިޔަވަޅު އަޅަންޖެހޭނެކަމަށް ވެސް މިނިސްޓަރ ދުންޔާ ވިދާޅުވިއެވެ.

en.body:
10 June 2014, Male'; Vice President Dr. Mohamed Jameel Ahmed has this evening returned to Male', on conclusion of an official visit to China, to attend the Opening Ceremony of the 2nd China-South Asia Expo, and the 9th China-South Asia Business Forum.

Meeting the local media at the Ibrahim Nasir International Airport upon his arrival, the Vice President stated that the official trip had been successful in furthering opportunities available to the investment, tourism, and renewable energy sectors in the Maldives.

The Vice President further noted that his official trip to China had re-affirmed international interest in investing in the Maldives, and had illuminated future trade opportunities between the Maldives and China.

Commenting on his meeting with the Governor of the Yunnan Province, H.E Mr. Li Jiheng, Vice President Jameel stated that the Governor had assured him of the commitment of the People's Government of Yunnan Province, to work with the Maldives in ‎strengthening areas of cooperation.

en.title: The Maldives begins its engagement at the 26th Session of the UN Human Rights Council
en.description: 10 June 2014, Geneva; The Maldives is participating in the 26th Session of the United Nations Human Rights Council which commenced today in Geneva.
en.body:
10 June 2014, Geneva; The Maldives is participating in the 26th Session of the United Nations Human Rights Council which commenced today in Geneva.

The Maldives will engage in the debate on important human rights country situations such as the Syrian Arab Republic, Palestine and DPRK. The Maldives today responded to the opening statement by the High Commissioner for Human Rights, Ms. Navi Pillay, who made her final statement to the Council. The Maldives condemned the gross human rights violation of the rights of Palestinian people and expansion of illegal settlements by Israel, the occupying power. The Maldives expressed grave concern at widespread and systematic violence in the Syrian Arab Republic and the lack of response and action from the international community.

In her statement delivered today, Her Excellency Ms. Iruthisham Adam, Ambassador/ Permanent Representative of the Republic of Maldives to the United Nations Offices in Geneva, reiterated the commitment of the Government of Maldives to the promotion and protection of human rights. She also reiterated challenges faced by Small Island Developing States (SIDS) such as the Maldives in implementing international obligations, and called for technical assistance to member states to better address them.

The Maldivian delegation will be involved in negotiations on a number of important human rights issues, specifically on rights of women, independence of judiciary, role of Parliament in the UPR process, climate change and human rights and other areas that are key priorities for the Maldives at the Council. The Maldives is in the core-group which is leading a high level panel "Power of Empowered Women 2014" with the participation of inspiring women leaders and entrepreneurs from around the world in a global conversation on equality and women's economic empowerment.

The Maldives expressed gratitude to Madam High Commissioner Pillay for her role and personal engagement as the High Commissioner during the past 6 years.

The Maldives is currently in its second term of membership of the Council. The Maldives is being represented at the session by the Permanent Mission of the Republic of Maldives to the United Nations Offices in Geneva.

ENDS

en.title: "We must celebrate the successes and plan for the road ahead in consolidating democracy" says Minister Dunya Maumoon
en.description: 9 June 2014, Male';"No nation is born a democracy. It is a process that evolves over time. Today as we mark the Tenth Anniversary of the launch of the Democratic Reform Agenda by President Gayoom, we must celebrate the successes and plan for the road ahead in consolidating democracy," says Minister…
en.body:
9 June 2014, Male';"No nation is born a democracy. It is a process that evolves over time. Today as we mark the Tenth Anniversary of the launch of the Democratic Reform Agenda by President Gayoom, we must celebrate the successes and plan for the road ahead in consolidating democracy," says Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ms. Dunya Maumoon. In her statement, the Foreign Minister congratulated the former President Maumoon Abdul Gayoom, who initiated and launched the Reform Agenda on 9 June 2004, and the current President Mr Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom for his valuable efforts in consolidating democracy and in cultivating the values of democracy in the society.

The Reform Agenda announced by the then President 10 years ago aimed to usher in a modern, liberal democracy with strengthened human rights safeguards and freedoms.Since then, the Maldives has made remarkable progress on achieving the lofty goals of the Agenda, of which the landmark constitution, which was ratified in 2008, was the most visible part of the programme.

On human rights reform, the Maldives has acceded to a wide-range of international agreements and treaties, including the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) with its Optional Protocol, and the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (ICESCR). Independent oversight bodies such as the Human Rights Commission of the Maldives and the Anti-Corruption Commission have been established.

On the political front, the Maldives is one of the most vibrant democracies in the region, with very active political participation. Additionally, there is a vibrant, vocal, and critical media with regular articles criticising Government policies and decisions, and an active civil society that contributes ideas, opinions, and criticism on a wide range of issues.

"Of course, there were bumps and setbacks along the way; our institutions are young, our processes and systems untested: the rights and their associated responsibilities new", observed the Minister, urging Maldivians to reflect on the challenges and the road ahead. The Minister called on all Maldivians to never let up the fight for democracy and human rights promotion in the country, and to never give up on strengthening the local institutions, empowering those institutions to administer justice and fairness, and to act with integrity, and to support upholding the rule of law above all.

"The peaceful transition of the Maldives, the related blossoming of human rights and the continued successes of our democratic journey, are home-grown achievements, made possible through the tireless dedication and sacrifices of ordinary Maldivians and the political will and sound policies of successive Governments. The success also reflects a strong, mutually respectful, and effective partnership between Maldives and the international community."

In conclusion, the Minister noted that "just like many others, the story of Maldives is still being written. It is up to every Maldivian, young and old, to contribute to a smooth progress, and a successful end of our journey towards consolidating democracy in our country."

ENDS

en.title: Foreign Minister Dunya sends a condolence message to Foreign Minister of Pakistan
en.description: 09 June 2014; Minister of Foreign Affairs, Her Excellency Ms Dunya Maumoon has sent a condolence message to His Excellency Mr. Sartaj Aziz, the Advisor to Prime Minister on National Security and Foreign Affairs of Pakistan condemning the attack on Karachi International Airport.
en.body:
09 June 2014; Minister of Foreign Affairs, Her Excellency Ms Dunya Maumoon has sent a condolence message to His Excellency Mr. Sartaj Aziz, the Advisor to Prime Minister on National Security and Foreign Affairs of Pakistan condemning the attack on Karachi International Airport.

Minister Dunya's message reads as follows:

"It was with profound sadness and deep sense of sympathy that I learnt of the brutal attacks on Karachi airport, which caused the loss of innocent lives and injury to many others."

"The Government and the People of Maldives condemn this act of terrorism in the strongest terms, and pledge our full support to the Government and the people of Pakistan. "

"At this time of national distress, the Government and the People of Maldives extend heartfelt condolences to the Government and the People of Pakistan and especially to the bereaved families."

ENDS.

dv.title: ޗައިނާ-ދެކުނު އޭޝިއާ 3 ވަނަ އެކްސްޕޮސިޝަނުގައި ޚާއްޞަ މެހުމާނެއްގެ ގޮތުގައި ރައީސް ޔާމިން ވަޑައިގަންނަވާނެކަމަށް ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު ދުންޔާ މައުމޫން ވިދާޅުވެއްޖެ
dv.description: ޗައިނާގެ ކުންމިންގް ގައި އޮންނަ ކުންމިން އިމްޕޯޓާއި އެކްސްޕޯޓާއި ބެހޭ ގޮތުން ބާއްވާ އެކްސްޕޮޒިޝަންގެ ޚާއްސަ މެހެމާނެއްގެ ގޮތުގައި ރައީސް ޔާމީން ބައިވެރިވެވަޑައިގަންނަވާނެ ކަމަށް ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު ދުންޔާ މައުމޫން ވިދާޅުވެއްޖެއެވެ.
dv.body:
ޗައިނާގެ ކުންމިންގް ގައި އޮންނަ ކުންމިން އިމްޕޯޓާއި އެކްސްޕޯޓާއި ބެހޭ ގޮތުން ބާއްވާ އެކްސްޕޮޒިޝަންގެ ޚާއްސަ މެހެމާނެއްގެ ގޮތުގައި ރައީސް ޔާމީން ބައިވެރިވެވަޑައިގަންނަވާނެ ކަމަށް ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު ދުންޔާ މައުމޫން ވިދާޅުވެއްޖެއެވެ.

މިކަން މީޑިއާއާއި ހިއްސާ ކުރައްވަމުން ދުންޔާ ވިދާޅުވީ މިމަހުގެ 11 ވަނަ ދުވަހު ރައީސް ޔާމީން ރަސްމީ ދަތުރުފުޅެއްގައި، މިއެކްސްޕޮޒިޝަންގައި ބައިވެރިވެވަޑައިގަތުމަށް ފުރާވަޑައިގަންނަވާނެކަމަށެވެ.

މިއެކްސްޕޮސިޝަނަކީ ވަރަށް މުހިއްމު ޖަލްސާތައް ބާއްވައި، ވަރަށް ގިނަ ޤައުމުތަކުގެ ވަފްދުތައް ބައިވެރިވާނެ އެކްސްޕޯއެއް ކަމަށާއި މި އެކްސްޕޯއަށް ރައީސް ޔާމީންއަށް ދަޢުވަތު ދެއްވާފައިވަނީ ޚާއްސަ މެހުމާނެއްގެ ގޮތުން ކަމަށް މިނިސްޓަރ ވިދާޅުވިއެވެ. އަދި މިދަޢުވަތު ސީދާ ރައީސްގެ އަތްޕުޅަށް އެރުއްވުމަށްޓަކައި ޗައިނާގެ ޔުނާން ޕްރޮވިންސްގެ ގަވަރުނަރު ރާއްޖެ އަށް ދަތުރުފުޅުކުރެއްވިކަން ދުންޔާ ފާހަގަކުރެއްވިއެވެ.

ދުންޔާ ވިދާޅުވީ ޗައިނާގައި ބާއްވާ މި އެކްސްޕޯގައި ބައިވެރިވެވަޑައިގަތުމަށް ރާއްޖޭގެ އިކޮނިމިކް މިނިސްޓަރު މުހައްމަދު ސަޢީދު، މާދަމާ ފުރާވަޑައިގަންނަވާނެ ކަމަށާއި މި ދަތުރުފުޅުގައި އެމަނިކުފާނާއެކު ވިޔަފާރިވެރިންގެ ވަފުދެއްވެސް ދަތުރުކުރައްވާނެ ކަމަށެވެ.

މިއަދުގެ ބޭއްވި ޕްރެސް ކޮންފަރެންސްގައި ދުންޔާ ވަނީ މާދަމާ އެކަމަނާ ޤަތަރަށް ކުރައްވާ ދަތުރުފުޅާ ބެހޭގޮތުން ވެސް މައުލޫމާތު ދެއްވާފައެވެ. މި ދަތުރުފުޅު ކުރައްވަނީ ރައީސުލް ޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ ޢަބުދުﷲ ޔާމީނުގެ ޚާރިޖީ ސިޔާސަތާ އެއްގޮތަށް އިސްލާމީ ޤައުމުތަކާއި ރާއްޖެއާ ދެމެދު އޮންނަ ގުޅުން ބަދަހި ކުރުމަށް ކަމަށާއި ދަތުރުފުޅުގައި ގަތަރު ސަރުކާރާ އެކު މަޝްވަރާ ކުރައްވާނީ ރާއްޖޭގެ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ވީހާ ވެސް ލުއި ގޮތަކަށް ކަންކަން ހަމަޖެއްސެވުމާއި މެދު ކަމަށް ވެސް އެކަމަނާ ވިދާޅުވިއެވެ. މިގޮތުން ވިސާގެ ކަންތައްތައް ފަސޭހަ ކުރުމާ ބެހޭ އެއްބަސްވުމެއްގައި ސޮއިކުރައްވާނެކަމަށް ދުންޔާ ވިދާޅުވިއެވެ.

މި ޕްރެސް ކޮންފަރެންސްގައި ދުންޔާ ވަނީ ދާދި ފަހުން ބޭއްވުނު އޯ.އައި.ސީ ސަމިޓާ ބެހޭގޮތުންވެސް މައުލޫމާތު ދެއްވާފައެވެ.

މި އަހަރުގެ ބައްދަވުން އޮތީ މެއި މަހުގެ 27 އިން 28 އަށް ކުވައިތުގައެވެ. މިސަމިޓުގައި މައިގަނޑުގޮތެއްގައި ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ފަރާތުން ވަކާލާތުކުރީ ޓެރަރިޒަމް ހުއްޓުވުމުގެ މުހިންމު ކަމާއި ގުޅޭގޮތުން މަސައްކަތްކުރުމާއި ބެހޭގޮތުންނާއި ޓެރަރިސްޓުން ދުނިޔޭގެ ޗާޓު އަލުން ކަނޑައެޅުމަށް ކުރަމުންދާ މަސައްކަތްތައް ހުއްޓުވުމާއި ބެހޭގޮތުންނެވެ.

އަދި މީގެ އިތުރުން ޓެރަރިސްޓު ގުރޫޕްތަކުން ސީރިއާ އަދި އިރާޤަށް ދޭ ހަމަލާތަކުގެ މައްޗަށާއި މުސްލިމުންނަށްދޭ އަނިޔާތަކުގެ މައްޗަށް ވެސް މަޝްވަރާކުރެވުނެވެ. އަދި ހަމަ އެހެންމެ، ހުޅަނގުގެ ޤައުމުތަކުން، މުސްލިމުންނަށް ވީތީ ކުރިމަތިކުރަމުންދާ ތަފާތުން ކުރުންތަކުގެ މައްޗައްވެސް އަލިއަޅުވާލެވުނެވެ.ޗައިނާ-ދެކުނު އޭޝިއާ 3 ވަނަ އެކްސްޕޮސިޝަނުގައި ޚާއްޞަ މެހުމާނެއްގެ ގޮތުގައި ރައީސް ޔާމިން ވަޑައިގަންނަވާނެކަމަށް ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު ދުންޔާ މައުމޫން ވިދާޅުވެއްޖެ

en.title: Vice President Meets the Governor of Yunnan Province ‎
en.description: 08 June 2014; During his official visit to China, H.E. Mohamed Jameel Ahmed, ‎Vice President of the Republic of Maldives had a very successful meeting ‎with H.E. Mr. Li Jiheng, Governor of Yunnan Province this evening.‎
en.body:
08 June 2014; During his official visit to China, H.E. Mohamed Jameel Ahmed, ‎Vice President of the Republic of Maldives had a very successful meeting ‎with H.E. Mr. Li Jiheng, Governor of Yunnan Province this evening.‎

Vice President H.E. Mr. Mohamed Jameel Ahmed noted the long-‎lasting close bilateral ties between the Maldives and China. The Vice ‎President further congratulated the Yunnan Governor on the development ‎of Kunming, specially emphasizing on the usage of renewable energy in the ‎city. Discussions were held on a wide array of areas where the two ‎countries could strengthen cooperation. H.E. Mr. Li Jiheng assured that the ‎People's Government of Yunnan Province will work with the Maldives in ‎strengthening areas of cooperation such as renewable energy, science and ‎technology, tourism, connectivity, economy and trade. ‎

The meeting was attended by Hon. Mohamed Saeed, Minister ‎of ‎Economic Development and Hon. Mr. ‎Abdulla Ameen, Minister at the ‎‎President's Office. Mr. Liu Ping, Senior Advisor of the People's ‎‎Government of Yunnan Province and other high level officials of the ‎‎Government of Yunnan Province also attend the meeting.‎

During the visit, the Vice President also met with H.E. Wang ‎Yang, Vice Premier of China. Discussions at the meeting were focused on ‎ways to further enhance bilateral cooperation between the two countries, in ‎areas such as trade and investment.‎

en.title: Government aims to serve the people with a strong mandate founded on economic transformation, youth empowerment and domestic security - Vice President
en.description: 08 June 2014; Vice President Dr. Mohamed Jameel Ahmed has stated that the Government aims to serve the Maldivian people with a strong mandate founded on economic transformation, youth empowerment and domestic security. The Vice President made this remark while speaking at the 9th China-South Asia…
en.body:
08 June 2014; Vice President Dr. Mohamed Jameel Ahmed has stated that the Government aims to serve the Maldivian people with a strong mandate founded on economic transformation, youth empowerment and domestic security. The Vice President made this remark while speaking at the 9th China-South Asia Business Forum, held in China.

The Vice President also underscored the high priority given by President Yameen to encourage foreign investment and capital towards the realisation of the Government's ambitious economic development programmes and projects.

In his speech, the Vice President noted the interest exhibited by Corporate China towards infrastructure development projects in the Maldives, and assured Chinese investors that every effort will be made by the Government to ensure that the investment climate in the Maldives was flexible and efficient.

Focusing on Sino-Maldives development ties, Vice President Jameel highlighted that China has been the number one tourism market in the Maldives for four consecutive years. He also indicated that tourist arrivals from China are forecasted to increase in the future.

ENDS.

en.title: Foreign investment is imperative for economic growth, private ‎sector development and wealth creation - Vice President ‎
en.description: 08 June 2014; Vice President Dr. Mohamed Jameel Ahmed has said that investment, ‎in particular foreign investment, is imperative for economic growth, private ‎sector development and wealth creation. The Vice President made this remark ‎while speaking at the inauguration of the 2nd China-South Asia…
en.body:
08 June 2014; Vice President Dr. Mohamed Jameel Ahmed has said that investment, ‎in particular foreign investment, is imperative for economic growth, private ‎sector development and wealth creation. The Vice President made this remark ‎while speaking at the inauguration of the 2nd China-South Asia Expo, held in ‎China. ‎

The Vice President underlined that while the Maldives currently has ‎the highest per-capita income in South Asia, a number of challenges, ‎shortcomings and deficiencies are present within the Maldivian economy. To ‎reverse the current economic fortunes, Vice President Jameel stated that the ‎current administration has opened its doors to foreign investors, by offering ‎incentives, concessions, cross subsidies, leverages and government ‎guarantees.‎

"Our Government firmly believes that broad-based, private sector-led ‎growth is essential to achieving faster development progress and to transform ‎the economy from where it is today", said the Vice President.‎
Continuing in this regard, Vice President Jameel highlighted key ‎projects on the Government's reform agenda, including iHavan, a broad ‎regional development project in the north of the country, as well as an ‎ambitious oil and gas exploration project, and plans to re-develop ‎Hulhumale' and the Ibrahim Nasir International Airport. ‎

The Vice President further stated that during the four decades, Sino-‎Maldives ties have grown from strength to strength, and re-affirmed that the ‎Government and people of Maldives cherish and attach great importance to ‎the close, historical relations between the two countries. ‎

ENDS.

en.title: The Maldives reaffirms its commitment to eliminate forced labour
en.description: 06 June 2014, Geneva, Switzerland; Speaking during the 103rd Session of the International Labour Conference, Permanent Representative of the Maldives/Ambassador, Her Excellency Ms. Iruthisham Adam reaffirmed the government's commitment to end all acts of forced labour in Maldives.
en.body:
06 June 2014, Geneva, Switzerland; Speaking during the 103rd Session of the International Labour Conference, Permanent Representative of the Maldives/Ambassador, Her Excellency Ms. Iruthisham Adam reaffirmed the government's commitment to end all acts of forced labour in Maldives.

Ambassador Adam stated that an Anti-Human Trafficking Act has been enacted in December 2013 in this regard, which makes trafficking of persons a criminal offence, including all types of forced labour and fraudulent recruitment. Ambassador Adam also informed of the government's commitment towards reforming its national labour regulations in line with the ILO standards to ensure that the rights of migrant worker population and also of the local workers is better protected.

Ambassador Adam further thanked the International Labour Organisation for its continued technical support to strengthen relevant institutions and protecting labour rights in the Maldives.

The 103rd session of the International Labour Organisation began on 28 May 2014 and will continue till 12 July 2014. A tripartite delegation consisting of government, employer and worker delegates are participating in the session from the Maldives.

ENDS

en.title: President has proposed for Parliamentary approval three names as ‎Heads of Diplomatic Missions
en.description: 05 June 2014, Male'; President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has today proposed three ‎officials for approval by the People's Majlis.‎
en.body:
05 June 2014, Male'; President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has today proposed three ‎officials for approval by the People's Majlis.‎

The nominated officials are:‎

‎- Mr. Abdulla Hameed as Non-Resident Ambassador to the United ‎Arab Emirates and the State of Kuwait

- Mr. Ahmed Shiaan as Ambassador to Belgium and the European ‎Union, and as Non-Resident High Commissioner to the United ‎Kingdom, and

- Dr. Mohamed Asim as Non-Resident High Commissioner to ‎Bangladesh ‎

Some of the proposals forwarded to the Majlis today are re-submissions ‎of names that were proposed to the 17th People's Majlis. The names ‎were sent back as no decisions were taken by the Majlis at its ‎conclusion.‎

ENDS.

en.title: High Commissioner Jaleel Presents his Letter of Credence to the President of Pakistan
en.description: 5 June 2014, Male'; New High Commissioner Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Maldives to Pakistan, H. E. Major ‎General (Retired) Moosa Ali Jaleel presented his letter of credence to the President of Pakistan H. E. Mr. Mamnoon Hussain today.
en.body:
5 June 2014, Male'; New High Commissioner Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Maldives to Pakistan, H. E. Major ‎General (Retired) Moosa Ali Jaleel presented his letter of credence to the President of Pakistan H. E. Mr. Mamnoon Hussain today.

High Commissioner Jaleel conveyed wells wishes from H.E. President Yameen to H. E. Mr. Mamnoon Hussain and thanked for all the assistance that Pakistan had provided to the Maldives in the past and reassured that relations between the Maldives and Pakistan will continue to flourish. He stressed that it was his highest priority to further strengthen relations between the two countries.

ENDS.

en.title: Timely global action a must in addressing climate change - ‎President Yameen
en.description: 05 June 2014, Male'; The President of Maldives, His Excellency Abdulla Yameen Abdul ‎Gayoom, in his message on the occasion of World Environment Day 2014, ‎has called for timely global action in addressing climate change. ‎
en.body:
05 June 2014, Male'; The President of Maldives, His Excellency Abdulla Yameen Abdul ‎Gayoom, in his message on the occasion of World Environment Day 2014, ‎has called for timely global action in addressing climate change. ‎

Quoting from the findings of the Working Group II of the ‎Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), the President emphasized ‎that changes in climate have caused impacts on natural and human systems ‎on all continent and across the oceans. ‎

"The quantity and quality of water resources are being affected. Climate ‎change is negatively impacting crop yields as well. Impacts from recent climate-‎related extremes reveal significant vulnerabilities and expose some ecosystems ‎and many human systems to current climate vulnerability. At the forefront of ‎those facing the effects of climate change are communities living in the world's ‎low-lying regions and small island states", the President highlighted.‎

Elaborating on the theme of this year's Environment Day, "Raise Your ‎Voice, Not the Sea Level", President Yameen welcomed the special focus ‎which will be afforded to small island nation states such as the Maldives, ‎particularly in line with the United Nations designating 2014 as the ‎International Year of Small Island Developing States. ‎

He also noted that the threats posed by sea level rise were initially ‎brought to global attention by Former President Maumoon Abdul Gayoom. ‎The President further noted that the Maldives has, from 1987 onwards, been ‎championing worldwide awareness and action against environmental ‎degradation.‎

ENDS.

en.title: "This year marks a pivotal point in our efforts to promote action on climate change and environmental degradation" - Minister Dunya Maumoon
en.description: 5 June 2014, Male': "This year marks a pivotal point in our efforts to promote action on climate change and environmental degradation" said H.E. Ms. Dunya Maumoon, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives. On the occasion of the World Environment Day, which is marked on 5 June of…
en.body:
5 June 2014, Male': "This year marks a pivotal point in our efforts to promote action on climate change and environmental degradation" said H.E. Ms. Dunya Maumoon, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives. On the occasion of the World Environment Day, which is marked on 5 June of every year, Minister Dunya highlighted the importance of taking concrete actions on all climate and environmental challenges before time runs out.

This year's theme "Small Islands and Climate Change" and the official slogan of this year "Raise Your Voice Not the Sea Level" are of special significance to the Maldives especially as Small Island States continuing to face unsurpassed challenges due to climate change and associated environmental challenges. The Minister called on all international partners, big and small, to unite in the combine their efforts in true partnerships, to achieve the sustainable development of SIDS as well as tackle the global environmental challenges of our time. In this regard, the Minister reiterated the Maldives's hope that key conferences and processes such as the Third International Conference on Small Island Developing States to be held in Apia, Samoa in September 2014, the negotiations of a new climate treaty at the Meetings of States Parties of the UNFCCC in Lima, Peru this year and in Paris, France in 2015, the negotiations of the Sustainable Development Goals that will formally begin this year, would be successful, and take into account the particular and unique vulnerabilities of SIDS.

Minister Dunya also highlighted that "the adverse impacts of environment degradation are the biggest challenge faced by the country today". For an island nation with 80% of its land less than two meters above sea level, climate change and its impacts are indescribable. The latest Report [by the IPCC] has proven thatclimate change is neither just an environmental issue nor a scientific thesis, but is of a question of the survival of each and every nation around the planet, irrespective of its size. It is our actions that would deteriorate these impacts.

The Minister also reiterated that the Maldives continues to bein the frontline while refusing to remain a victim, and have been an agent of change in addressing environmental issues. The Maldives is currently in the process of developing a low carbon development strategy which paints a promising picture not only for the nation but the world. Internationally, the Maldives has led efforts to emphasize the links between human rights and climate change, as well as the plight of small states. However, the Minister noted that the Maldives, and any other country working alone would not be able to deliver durable solutions, but the world must unite to provide lasting and comprehensive solutions to the environmental challenges of our times. "It is the hope of the Maldives, along with a number of other states, that the world remains interested and continues to seek to deliver solutions and work together."

ENDS

en.title: Vice President Departs on an Official Visit to China
en.description: 04 June 2014; Vice President Dr. Mohamed Jameel Ahmed has this evening ‎departed on an official visit to China. During this official visit, he will be ‎attending the Opening Ceremony of the 2nd China-South Asia Expo, and the ‎‎9th China-South Asia Business Forum. The Vice President is also…
en.body:
04 June 2014; Vice President Dr. Mohamed Jameel Ahmed has this evening ‎departed on an official visit to China. During this official visit, he will be ‎attending the Opening Ceremony of the 2nd China-South Asia Expo, and the ‎‎9th China-South Asia Business Forum. The Vice President is also ‎scheduled to meet with the Vice Premier of China, H.E Wang Yang. ‎

Meeting the local media at the Ibrahim Naseer International ‎Airport prior to his departure, Vice President Jameel said that he will be ‎meeting with the Chinese business community, in order to seek potential ‎investors for various development projects in the Maldives.‎

Continuing in this regard, the Vice President stated that he will be ‎discussing the Government's reform agenda with the Chinese Government, ‎including housing development projects, the integrated development ‎project, iHavan, in the north of the country, and airport development ‎initiatives. Vice President Jameel further stated that the Chinese ‎Government has expressed its keenness in cooperating with the Maldives ‎on these development projects.‎

Vice President Jameel is accompanied by Minister at the ‎President's Office, Hon. Abdulla Ameen.‎

en.title: Maldives High Commission in Malaysia holds dialogue with Universities
en.description: 04 June 2014, Kuala Lumpur; The High Commission of Maldives in Malaysia today held a dialogue and discussion meeting with key educational institutions of Kuala Lumpur.
en.body:
04 June 2014, Kuala Lumpur; The High Commission of Maldives in Malaysia today held a dialogue and discussion meeting with key educational institutions of Kuala Lumpur.

The meeting, held at the High Commission, yesterday was focused on building a good rapport with the institutions and communicating the challenges faced by Maldivian students during their study in Malaysia and exchange views on how these can be overcome.

Opening the discussion, Counsellor at the Mission Ms. Ghaniya Abdul Ghafoor thanked the Universities and Colleges for their continued cooperation. During the dialogue it was highlighted that Maldives played a major part in developing Malaysia as an educational hub of the region, and most importantly, that the increased number of Maldivian students in Malaysia was a result of the success of the marketing fairs conducted between the two countries.

The High Commission also urged the institutions to provide accurate information regarding immigration processes so that students and their guardians could make informed decisions before their travel to Malaysia.

Discussions also focused on the hardships faced by Maldivian students when their passports are not on them during visa processing. Views were exchanged on how these critical issues could be solved with a view to ensuring the welfare of students. Thirteen Universities and Colleges participated in today's dialogue. These include, Sunway University, Monash University, University Tun Razak, Asia Pacific University, UCSI University, Taylors University, Segi University, International Medical University, KBU International College, Infrastructure University Kuala Lumpur, University of Nottingham, Nilai university and KDU. The High Commission will be holding such dialogue forums during the course of the year to facilitate a smoother stay for Maldivian students in Malaysia.

ENDS.

en.title: Ambassador Hameed calls on the State Minister of Foreign Affairs of UAE
en.description: 04 June 2014, UAE; Ambassador at Large, His Excellency Mr. Abdulla Hameed who is currently on an Official Visit to UAE has today called on the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs of UAE, His Excellency Dr. Anwar Mohammed Gargash.
en.body:
04 June 2014, UAE; Ambassador at Large, His Excellency Mr. Abdulla Hameed who is currently on an Official Visit to UAE has today called on the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs of UAE, His Excellency Dr. Anwar Mohammed Gargash.

At the meeting held, Ambassador Hameed extended greetings and good wishes from the Government and the people of Maldives to the Government and the people of UAE.

Furthermore, Ambassador Hameed remarked at the value attached by the Government of Maldives in respect of the bilateral ties that exist between the two countries, and highlighted the attributes of shared values, and mutual respect, that underlie the close relations.

During the meeting, Ambassador and State Minister discussed ways of further strengthening the existing close relations between the Maldives and UAE, with an emphasis on greater economic cooperation in the areas of trade, investment and education.

Today, Ambassador also met the Director General of Abu Dhabi Fund, Mr. Mohamed Saif Al Suwaidi and Director of Diplomatic Affairs of UAE Foreign Ministry, Mr. Abdul Wahhab Al Najjar.

Ambassador Hameed departed to UAE on 3 June 2014 to undertake the official visit and will return to Maldives on 6 June 2014.

ENDS.

en.title: President Sends a Message of Condolence to Prime ‎Minister of India
en.description: 04 June 2014, Male'; President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has sent a message of condolence ‎to Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, following the tragic demise ‎of Gopinath Munde, India's Minister for Rural Development and senior ‎leader of the BJP.‎
en.body:
04 June 2014, Male'; President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has sent a message of condolence ‎to Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, following the tragic demise ‎of Gopinath Munde, India's Minister for Rural Development and senior ‎leader of the BJP.‎

The President's message reads as follows:‎

‎"It is with profound sorrow and sadness that I received the news of the tragic ‎demise of Gopinath Munde, India's Minister for Rural Development and ‎senior leader of the BJP."‎

‎"The late Shri Munde will surely be fondly remembered as a true champion of ‎democracy and fundamental rights for the less privileged, especially in his ‎beloved State of Maharastra. On your invitation, I, of course, had the honour ‎of personally witnessing the historic swearing-in to office of your Union ‎Cabinet of Ministers, which included Shri Gopinath Munde. I can, therefore, ‎guage your deep sorrow at the loss of a close friend and comrade."‎

‎"At this time of national mourning in India, the Government and the people ‎of the Maldives and I personally join you, and the Government and people of ‎India, in sharing your profound grief. Our sympathies also go out to the ‎entire BJP family, of which Shri Munde was an integral member until his ‎untimely passing away. Furthermore, please convey my sincere condolences ‎to the bereaved family."‎

ENDS.

en.title: New Sudanese Ambassador presents credentials to the President
en.description: 04 June 2014, Male'; The new Sudanese Ambassador accredited to the Maldives, His ‎Excellency Dr. Hassan Eisa Hassan Al Talib presented his letter of credence ‎to President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom this morning.‎
en.body:
04 June 2014, Male'; The new Sudanese Ambassador accredited to the Maldives, His ‎Excellency Dr. Hassan Eisa Hassan Al Talib presented his letter of credence ‎to President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom this morning.‎

At the ceremony held at the President's Office to present ‎credentials, President Yameen congratulated Ambassador Al Talib on the ‎commencement of his term. Following the ceremony, the President and the ‎‎Ambassador discussed ways to strengthening existing bilateral ties between ‎the Maldives and Sudan, and explored avenues for further cooperation ‎between the two countries. Ambassador Al Talib commented on the special ‎fraternal relationship between the Maldives and Sudan, with both countries ‎being Muslim nations, and affirmed his commitment to enhancing these ties ‎during his term of office. President Yameen recalled the longstanding ‎cordial ties between the two countries, and emphasized his wish for ‎bilateral collaborative efforts to improve further in the time ahead.‎

The meeting was attended by the Minister at the President's Office, ‎Hon. Mohamed Hussain Shareef, Foreign Secretary, Dr. Ali Naseer ‎Mohamed, and the Military Attaché at the Sudanese Embassy in India, Mr. ‎A. Hamid.‎

ENDS.

en.title: Italian Ambassador Calls on the President
en.description: 04 June 2014, Male'; Ambassador of Italy accredited to the Maldives, His Excellency Fabrizio ‎Pio Arpea has paid a courtesy call on President Abdulla Yameen Abdul ‎Gayoom. The meeting was held this morning at the President's Office.‎
en.body:
04 June 2014, Male'; Ambassador of Italy accredited to the Maldives, His Excellency Fabrizio ‎Pio Arpea has paid a courtesy call on President Abdulla Yameen Abdul ‎Gayoom. The meeting was held this morning at the President's Office.‎

At the meeting, the President Yameen and the Ambassador Arpea ‎discussed bilateral relations between the two countries and expressed ‎hopes of further strengthening these relations. ‎ ‎In this regard, discussions ‎were held on extending cooperation between ‎the ‎two countries in ‎education, health and tourism sectors.‎

Underscoring his Government's agenda for economic development and ‎expansion of opportunities for trade and investment, President Yameen ‎briefed Ambassador Arpea ‎ on the Government strategies to create a more ‎favourable foreign investment climate in the country. President Yameen ‎also expressed his appreciation for Italy's continued assistance ‎and ‎support to the socio-economic ‎development of the Maldives. ‎

Highlighting the close relationship the Maldives has with Italy, ‎Ambassador Arpea reassured of his Government's continuous support and ‎cooperation to the Maldives. He also noted that, after recent less ‎favourable trends in tourism arrival numbers from Italy as a result of the ‎economic crunch across Europe, there is growing enthusiasm in traveling ‎abroad, including sought-after destinations such as the Maldives.‎

President Yameen was joined at the call by the Minister at the President's ‎Office, Hon. Mohamed ‎Hussain Shareef, and Foreign Secretary Dr. Ali ‎Naseer Mohamed.‎

ENDS.

en.title: Chief Observer of the EU Election Observer Mission calls on the Foreign Minister
en.description: 03 June 2014, Male'; Chief Observer of the EU Election Observer Mission, His Excellency Mr Eduard Kukan called on the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon, today.
en.body:
03 June 2014, Male'; Chief Observer of the EU Election Observer Mission, His Excellency Mr Eduard Kukan called on the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon, today.

At the meeting held this afternoon, His Excellency Mr Eduard Kukan presented the Report of the EU Election Observer Mission and expressed appreciation for the cooperation extended to them by the Government of Maldives. Mr. Kukan highlighted that the entire electoral process was generally well administered and was completed smoothly.

Minister Dunya noted with appreciation the important work undertaken by the EU Observer Mission and extended assurances that the Government will work with relevant authorities to ensure that the election procedures are further strengthened in the future. She also expressed hope that the country will continue to receive support and cooperation from the EU for future elections.

Minister Dunya was accompanied by Ms. Zenysha Zaki, Director of the Foreign Ministry of the Maldives.

en.title: President congratulates President-elect of Egypt
en.description: 02 June 2014, Male'; President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has sent a congratulatory message to the President-elect of Egypt, His Excellency Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, following his success in Egypt's recent presidential elections.
en.body:
02 June 2014, Male'; President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has sent a congratulatory message to the President-elect of Egypt, His Excellency Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, following his success in Egypt's recent presidential elections.

The President's message reads as follows:

"On behalf of the Government and the people of the Republic of Maldives and on my own behalf, it gives me great pleasure to extend to you heartfelt congratulations on your historic landslide victory in the recent presidential elections of the Arab Republic of Egypt. I firmly believe that the overwhelming majority that you had secured in the polls is an unmistakable mandate from the Egyptian people for you to forge ahead confidently with your vision for a peaceful, prosperous and progressive Egypt."

"As a longstanding friend and ally, the Maldives is delighted that Egypt is entering a new era of optimism, both nationally and internationally. I am convinced that, under your wise leadership, the Egyptian government will return the country to its rightful place among the region's most successful nations. The Maldives will, of course, stand shoulder to shoulder with the Egyptian people as they pursue their aspirations to consolidate their democratic rights, strengthen governance institutions and reinvigorate the economy."

"I wish you fortitude and strong resolve in discharging the important duties of your position, as well as new heights of progress and prosperity to Egypt and its people. While expressing the hope that the fraternal relations existing between our two countries will be further strengthened in the years to come, allow me also to convey to Your Excellency my personal good wishes for your health and well-being."

ENDS.

en.title: New Pakistani High Commissioner presents credentials to the President
en.description: 02 June 2014, Male'; The new Pakistani High Commissioner accredited to the Maldives, His Excellency Syed Sail Abbas presented his letter of credence to President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom this morning.
en.body:
02 June 2014, Male'; The new Pakistani High Commissioner accredited to the Maldives, His Excellency Syed Sail Abbas presented his letter of credence to President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom this morning.

At the ceremony held at the President's Office to present the credentials, President Yameen congratulated High Commissioner Abbas on the commencement of his term. Following the ceremony, the President and the ‎High Commissioner discussed ways to further enhance existing close friendly relations between the Maldives and Pakistan, ‎and explored new avenues ‎for cooperation, including healthcare, sports, agriculture, ‎construction, and commerce and trade.

Recalling the historic visit of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif to India to attend the oath-taking of the new Indian Prime Minister, President Yameen highlighted the importance of Pakistan and India taking the leadership in forging greater regional cooperation among the eight-members of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC). He noted the importance of marginalizing bilateral disputes from the SAARC agenda, in presenting the Association as a strong regional bloc. On this point, the President elaborated on the need to encourage bilateral and trilateral pacts within SAARC, which would complement the existing SAFTA arrangements, to ensure that the volume of trade within the region will also benefit smaller member states.

President Yameen said that he is keenly looking forward to his upcoming State Visit to Pakistan, including opportunities to meet with the Pakistani President Manmoon Hussain and Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif.

High Commissioner Syed Sail Abbas assured the President of his firm commitment to strengthen bilateral ties during his tenure as the resident Pakistani High Commissioner to the Maldives, and proposed further initiatives to improve export-import collaboration between private sectors of both countries. He expressed his confidence that the upcoming presidential visit to Pakistan would pave the way for further enhancement of ties and socioeconomic collaboration in new fields.

The new Pakistani High Commissioner emphasized the important role of existing Pakistani investments in the Maldives, including the contribution of Habib Bank Limited. He concurred with the President's view that trade and commerce encompassed important avenues for future collaboration. On the topic of SAARC, High Commissioner Abbas highlighted the high priority that Pakistan continued to attach to strengthen regional ties and noted that a stronger SAARC is the way forward in enhancing peace, progress, and prosperity in the region.

The meeting was attended by Minister of Foreign Affairs, Hon. Dunya Maumoon, Minister at the President's Office, Hon. Mohamed Hussain Shareef and Mr. Zafar Anjum Iqbal, Head of Chancery at the High Commission of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan in Male'.

ENDS.

Minister Dunya's message reads as follows:

"I am deeply grieved to hear the news of the passing away of His Royal Highness Sultan Azian Muhibbuddin Shah Ibni Almarhum Sultan Yussuff Izzuddin Shah Ghafarullahu-Lah, the 34th Sultan of the State of Perak Darul Ridzuan and the 9th Yang di-Pertuan Agong of Malaysia. (King of Malaysia from 26th April 1989 to 25th April 1994). May Almighty Allah grant him eternal paradise."

"On this very sad occasion, I would like to extend, on behalf of the Government and the people of the Maldives and on my own behalf, our profound condolences to Your Excellency, the Government and friendly people of Malaysia. "

"Please also convey my sincere condolences to the members of the bereaved family."

en.title: "We can safeguard our independence by becoming more resilient" says Minister of Foreign Affairs
en.description: 30 May 2014, Male'; "We can safeguard our independence by becoming more resilient and self-sufficient" said Her Excellency Ms Dunya Maumoon, Minister of Foreign Affairs. Speaking on the occasion of Martyrs Day, Minister Dunya urged all Maldivians to "not back down from our responsibility to protect…
en.body:
30 May 2014, Male'; "We can safeguard our independence by becoming more resilient and self-sufficient" said Her Excellency Ms Dunya Maumoon, Minister of Foreign Affairs. Speaking on the occasion of Martyrs Day, Minister Dunya urged all Maldivians to "not back down from our responsibility to protect our nation".

In her address to the nation, Minister Dunya further asserted that the responsibility to protect and safeguard the independence and heritage of their country was a responsibility of every Maldivian inherited from their forefathers. Their ultimate sacrifice in fulfilling this responsibility is the reason why martyrs are regarded so highly, Minister Dunya asserted. Therefore, while remembering several martyrs who had sacrificed their lives and livelihoods for the future of the nation, she urged Maldivians to not forsake their sacrifice, and work endlessly to protect the independence and heritage of the country.

Minister Dunya also highlighted the important contributions that women make to society and to protecting and safeguarding a country's independence. She noted that the contributions of both men and women are necessary for the development of the country and to improve the economic resilience of the country.

Martyrs Day is celebrated on the first of Sha'aban, the eighth month of the Hijri calendar, every year. The day commemorates the day on which Ah-Sultan Ali the sixth was martyred while fighting for the independence of the country, 470 years back.

en.title: Maldives signs Memorandum of Understanding on Peacekeepers
en.description: 29 May 2014, UN Headquarters, New York: Today, Ambassador Ahmed Sareer signed a Memorandum of Understanding on Contributions to the United Nations Stand-by Arrangements System, paving the way for the deployment of Maldivian UN military observers and peacekeepers. Signing on behalf of the United…
en.body:
29 May 2014, UN Headquarters, New York: Today, Ambassador Ahmed Sareer signed a Memorandum of Understanding on Contributions to the United Nations Stand-by Arrangements System, paving the way for the deployment of Maldivian UN military observers and peacekeepers. Signing on behalf of the United Nations, Under-Secretary-General Hervé Ladsous remarked that this was a "momentous day for the Republic of Maldives and the Maldivian people."

Noting the upcoming Golden Jubilee marking the 50th anniversary of relations between the Maldives and the United Nations, Ambassador Sareer stated that "this agreement marks a new era in relations between the Maldives and the UN. With the maturation of the Maldivian State, we look forward to taking up the mantle of leadership in all of our international endeavors. No matter how small the nation, all have an obligation to maintaining and sustaining the security of populations across the globe."

As this is the first agreement of its kind for the Maldives, a small contingent of military observers and infantry personnel will be deployed over the next two years. Discussing the unique strengths of the Maldives, USG Hervé Ladsous commented that "Maldives' experience in protecting its incredibly porous border provides invaluable expertise in addressing modern threats, including the prevention of; piracy, trafficking and maritime conflict."

The ceremony was also attended by Salim Waheed, Deputy Permanent Representative to the United Nations.

ENDS

en.title: "NAM should continue to enhance solidarity, to unite to deliver peace and prosperity for all" Foreign Secretary
en.description: 28 May 2014; Foreign Secretary Dr. Ali Naseer Mohamed has called on the Non-Aligned Movement to be "a source of support for encouraging democracies", and "a source of courage for the weakest and the smallest" nations in the international system. The Foreign Secretary made these calls at his…
en.body:
28 May 2014; Foreign Secretary Dr. Ali Naseer Mohamed has called on the Non-Aligned Movement to be "a source of support for encouraging democracies", and "a source of courage for the weakest and the smallest" nations in the international system. The Foreign Secretary made these calls at his statement delivered last night at the 17th NAM Conference held in Algiers, Algeria.

On his statement, the Foreign Secretary also said that in the contemporary would politics, it is not the size that matters, but "good ideas, and smart ideas, and the ability of nations to transform, to adapt, and to accommodate to changing dynamics".

The Foreign Secretary recalled some of the important initiatives that the Maldives has successfully launched in the international arena, including its efforts in drawing the world's attention to climate change, the security of small states, and human dimension of climate change. The Foreign Secretary said that the Maldives has been successful in these initiatives "not because of its purchasing power parity, but because of its ability to advocate new ideas in addressing common challenges".

The Foreign Secretary is heading the Maldives delegation at the Ministerial Conference, which commenced in Algiers yesterday. He is accompanied by Ms Nizwee Rasheed, Assistant Director of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

ENDS.

en.title: President sends message of sympathy to the President of China
en.description: 28 May 2014, Male'; President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has sent a message of sympathy to President Xi Jinping of China, following the terrorist attack in a market in Urumqi, China.
en.body:
28 May 2014, Male'; President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has sent a message of sympathy to President Xi Jinping of China, following the terrorist attack in a market in Urumqi, China.

The President's message reads as follows:

"It is with deep shock and sorrow that the Government and the people of the Maldives and I learnt about the heinous attack in a market in the northwest Chinese city of Urumqi, causing tragic loss of innocent lives and grievous injury to many. The Government and the people of the Maldives condemn in the strongest terms this cowardly act, and we express our firm solidarity with the People's Republic of China in all its efforts to maintain peace and harmony."

"The Maldives stands firm in its commitment to the fight against the global menace of terrorism, and will continue to work closely with the People's Republic of China and the international community as a whole in eliminating the scourge of terrorism."

"On this sad occasion of national grief, the government and the people of the Maldives and I pledge our full support and extend our deepest sympathy to you, the Government and the people of China, especially to those who were directly affected by the attack. Please also convey our sincere condolences to the members of the bereaved families."

ENDS.

en.title: President concludes Official Visit to India
en.description: 28 May 2014; President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has arrived this ‎evening on conclusion of his official visit to India. The President's visit was ‎made on the invitation of the Indian government to attend the inauguration ‎ceremony of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.‎
en.body:
28 May 2014; President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has arrived this ‎evening on conclusion of his official visit to India. The President's visit was ‎made on the invitation of the Indian government to attend the inauguration ‎ceremony of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.‎

Speaking to the local media on arrival at the Ibrahim Nasir ‎International Airport, the President highlighted the warm and gracious ‎hospitality extended to him and his delegation by the Indian government ‎during their stay in India. Additionally, President Yameen stated that both ‎governments had re-affirmed their commitment to further consolidating ‎Indo-Maldivian relations.‎

The President also briefed the media on his discussions with Prime ‎Minister Modi during their meeting this morning, which focused on key ‎bilateral issues, the future of the South Asian Association of Regional ‎Cooperation (SAARC), and issues of regional security.‎

President Yameen further highlighted that he had extended an ‎invitation to the newly-elected Indian Prime Minister to visit the Maldives ‎next year to take part in the ‘Golden Jubilee' celebrations marking 50 years ‎of the country's independence. Continuing in this regard, the President ‎noted that Sri Lankan President Mahinda Rajapaksa had also accepted the ‎government's invitation to visit the Maldives to take part in the ‘Golden ‎Jubilee' Independence Day festivities. ‎

Recalling his meeting this morning with senior officials of India's ‎ruling Bharatiya Janatha Party, President Yameen noted that BJP leaders ‎were committed to establishing strong ties with the incumbent Progressive ‎Party of Maldives (PPM).‎

ENDS.

en.title: President Yameen Meets with Senior Officials of Bharatiya Janatha Party
en.description: 27 May 2014; President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has met with senior officials from the ruling Bharatiya Janatha Party (BJP) of India.
en.body:
27 May 2014; President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has met with senior officials from the ruling Bharatiya Janatha Party (BJP) of India.

At the meeting held this afternoon at the hotel in which the Maldivian President is residing at, the President highlighted the key issues discussed during his meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. In this regard, the President reaffirmed Maldives' commitment to further strengthening bilateral relations with India.

The President conveyed his appreciation for receiving an invitation to attend ‎the momentous occasion of the inauguration of the New Prime Minister. ‎President Yameen also expressed hope that the historic move to extend invitation to all SAARC leaders would further enhance regional ties.

Deliberating the importance of promoting relations and understanding among the SAARC countries, President Yameen underscored the pivotal role played by India in regional affairs. Continuing in this line, President Yameen thanked the Government of India for the generous assistances provided to the Maldives during times of need.

Recalling the previous administration of BJP, President Yameen lauded support to the policies of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee. Continuing on, President Yameen noted the significant positive effects of the policies on regional growth.

Noting the Indian Government resolve to strengthen ties with other friendly nations, the BJP officials highlighted the long-standing bilateral relations that exist between the Maldives and India.

ENDS

en.title: President Yameen Reaffirms Commitment to Further Strengthening Relations with India
en.description: 27 May 2014; In his meeting with the newly elected Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, President Yameen has reaffirmed the government's commitment to further strengthening bilateral relations with India. The meeting was held this morning at Hyderabad House, New Delhi.
en.body:
27 May 2014; In his meeting with the newly elected Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, President Yameen has reaffirmed the government's commitment to further strengthening bilateral relations with India. The meeting was held this morning at Hyderabad House, New Delhi.

Prime Minister Modi extended a warm welcome to President Yameen to India. President Yameen also thanked the Prime Minister of India for the warm and gracious hospitality extended to him and members of his delegation during their stay.

Underscored by shared values and geographical contiguity between the two countries, President Yameen expressed his confidence that the long-standing close relations between Maldives and India would continue to be further strengthened under Prime Minister Modi's tenure. He also stated that, in shaping Maldivian foreign policy, India's interests and status as a global leader would continue to be accorded the highest respect.

President Yameen noted that India was the first country to establish diplomatic relations with the Maldives following its independence in 1965, highlighting the strong historical ties between the two nations.

In discussing the future of the South Asian Association of Regional Cooperation (SAARC), President Yameen noted that the invitation extended to the leaders of SAARC, particularly Pakistan's Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif, was indicative of the significance afforded to the regional organization by Prime Minister Modi. The Indian Prime Minister also remarked that all SAARC countries should prioritize strengthening regional relations in order to mutually realize their developmental aspirations, and contribute to the prosperity and security of the South Asian region.

In the meeting today, Prime Minister Modi also affirmed the Indian government's commitment to providing further higher education opportunities to Maldivian students, while also lending the Indian government's full support to the tourism sector in the Maldives.

President Yameen was joined at the meeting by Minister of Foreign Affairs, Hon. Dunya Maumoon, Ministers at the President's Office, Hon. Mohamed Hussain Shareef and Hon. Abdulla Ameen, High Commissioner of Maldives to India Mr. Mohamed Naseer, and Spokesperson at the President's Office Mr. Ibrahim Muaz Ali. Prime Minister Modi was accompanied at the call by the Indian Minister of External Affairs Ms. Sushma Swaraj, Foreign Secretary Mrs. Sujatha Singh and the Indian High Commissioner to the Maldives Mr. Rajeev Sahare.

ENDS.

en.title: Maldives participates in the 17th Ministerial Meeting of Foreign Ministers of Non-Aligned Countries
en.description: 27 May 2014, Male': Maldives is participating in the 17th Ministerial Meeting of Foreign Ministers of Non-Aligned Countries and the Senior Officials Meeting being held from 26 to 29 May 2014 at Algiers, Algeria. The Maldives delegation to the Meeting is headed by His Excellency Dr. Ali Naseer…
en.body:
27 May 2014, Male': Maldives is participating in the 17th Ministerial Meeting of Foreign Ministers of Non-Aligned Countries and the Senior Officials Meeting being held from 26 to 29 May 2014 at Algiers, Algeria. The Maldives delegation to the Meeting is headed by His Excellency Dr. Ali Naseer Mohamed, Foreign Secretary at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Ms. Nizwee Rasheed, Assistant Director at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The 17th Ministerial Meeting of Foreign Ministers of Non-Aligned Countries is set to review the progress and implementation of the Tehran Plan of Action adopted at the XVI Summit of Heads of State and Government of the Non-Aligned Movement held in 2012 in Tehran, the Islamic Republic of Iran, and to prepare for the upcoming NAM Summit in Caracas, the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, in 2015, as well as to address existing, new and emerging issues of collective concern and interest of the Non-Aligned Movement, under the theme "Enhanced Solidarity for Peace and Prosperity". The Foreign Secretary will deliver a statement at the General Debate of the Ministerial Meeting on 28 May 2014. The statement will focus on the continued relevance of the founding principles of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) and the need to bring together the different expertise and knowledge to enhance solidarity for peace and prosperity.

The Non-Aligned Movement, or NAM, is an international organization of 120 states which consider themselves not formally aligned with or against any major power bloc. NAM has generally concerned itself with issues of sovereignty, territorial integrity, and security, decolonisation, racism, all forms of foreign aggression, occupation, domination, interference or hegemony. Maldives has participated in all Meetings of NAM since the 5th summit.

ENDS

en.title: Foreign Minister Dunya congratulates the new Minister of External Affairs of India
en.description: 27 May 2014; Minister of Foreign Affairs Ms. Dunya Maumoon has sent a congratulatory message to the Minister of External Affairs of the Republic of India, H.E. Ms. Sushma Swaraj, following her appointment.
en.body:
27 May 2014; Minister of Foreign Affairs Ms. Dunya Maumoon has sent a congratulatory message to the Minister of External Affairs of the Republic of India, H.E. Ms. Sushma Swaraj, following her appointment.

Minister Dunya's message to Minister Sushmareads as follows:

"It is my pleasure to extend to you my warmest congratulations on your appointment as the Minister of External Affairs of India. As you assume your challenging responsibilities, I wish to convey to you my best wishes for your success."

"As a close friend and neighbour, the Maldives, attaches high importance to the unique relationship with India.I, therefore, remain confident that the cooperation that exists between the Maldives and India will be further strengthened and developed during your term in office."

"I look forward to working closely with you in enhancing our cooperation for the benefit of the people of both our countries. I would also like to take this opportunity to extend an invitation to visit Maldives at Your Excellency's convenience."

ENDS.

en.body:
26 May 2014; President of the Republic of Maldives, His Excellency Mr. Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has called on the President of Sri Lanka, His Excellency Mr. Mahinda Rajapaksa on the sidelines of the ongoing official visit to India, and thanked the Sri Lankan President for the recent strengthening of the bilateral ties between the two countries.

At the meeting, which was held this afternoon, President Yameen highlighted the longstanding friendly relations between Sri Lanka and Maldives, and noted the success of the President's maiden visit to Sri Lanka in January, that has led to further enhancing of the bilateral ties that exist between two countries.

Further at the discussions, Presidnet Yameen and the Sri Lankan President, concurred that the initiative taken on inviting SAARC Heads of States to the Inaugural Ceremony of Prime Minister Mordi, was an encouraging gesture, and a positive step towards maintaining the existing friendly relations and collaboration amongst the member states.

en.title: Visiting World Bank officials call on the President
en.description: 25 May 2014, Male'; Executive Director of the World Bank, Dr. Mirza Hassan, and the Vice President of the World Bank, Mr. Philippe Le Houérou, who are on review mission to the Maldives, have paid a courtesy call on President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom.
en.body:
25 May 2014, Male'; Executive Director of the World Bank, Dr. Mirza Hassan, and the Vice President of the World Bank, Mr. Philippe Le Houérou, who are on review mission to the Maldives, have paid a courtesy call on President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom.

At the meeting held at the President's Office this morning, the President briefed Dr. Hassan and Mr. Houérou on the Government's economic and fiscal policies. He briefed the World Bank delegation on measures being implemented by the government towards fiscal stability, and outlined his vision to improve existing reserves. He also noted the initiative to lower MRR and attract foreign investment towards infrastructure projects outlined in the Government's manifesto. Elaborating on the Government's plans to develop economic growth cluster zones, the President said that the Government would prioritize youth employment and raising standards of living.

The visiting World Bank officials thanked the President for his valuable input, which they highlighted, would form the base of their future collaborations with the Maldives. They assured the President that the World Bank would continue to share their knowledge, expertise and resources with the Maldives, and would work closely with the Ministry of Finance and Treasury and the Maldives Monetary Authority, in the time ahead. They also informed the President of the ongoing efforts to formulate a long-term programme plan for the Maldives, which would complement the President's economic growth commitments. They went on to note the importance of shore protection of Maldivian island communities, the establishment of safe and efficient waste disposal facilities across the nation, and the introduction of cleaner energy alternatives in catering for the growing demands of the population as featuring among key areas of focus in the country's continued development. They also assured that MIGA and IFS would also continue to enhance their collaborations with the Maldives, particularly in attracting further foreign investment towards earmarked mega projects of the Government.

President Yameen was joined at this morning's meeting by Hon. Abdulla Jihad, Minister of Finance and Treasury and Ministers at the President's Office, Hon. Abdulla Ameen and Hon. Mohamed Hussain Shareef.

en.title: President sends message of sympathy to the President of Bangladesh
en.description: 19 May 2014, Male'; President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has sent a message of sympathy ‎to President M.D. Abdul Hamid of Bangladesh, following the sinking of a ‎ferry boat in Meghna River.‎
en.body:
19 May 2014, Male'; President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has sent a message of sympathy ‎to President M.D. Abdul Hamid of Bangladesh, following the sinking of a ‎ferry boat in Meghna River.‎

The President's message read as follows;‎

"It is with sorrow and dismay that I learnt of the tragic incident of a ‎passenger ferry capsizing in the Meghna River, causing the loss of many ‎innocent lives and injury to hundreds of people. While the search for ‎survivors continues, we pray that, of those that remain unaccounted for so ‎far, more victims can be saved."‎

"At this time of tragedy, the Government and the people of the Maldives join ‎me in conveying our profound sympathy to Your Excellency, the ‎Government and the brotherly people of Bangladesh, particularly the families ‎of the bereaved, and offer prayers to those who have been injured in this ‎catastrophe. I wish the recovery efforts every success and commend the ‎tenacity of the Bangladeshi people in the face of such tragedy."‎

"I am confident that with the characteristic courage and fortitude of your ‎people, they will be able to find the solace to overcome their sorrow. The ‎Government and the people of the Maldives stand in solidarity with you, and ‎the people of Bangladesh, in coming to terms with this tragedy."‎

ENDS.

en.title: President sends message of sympathy to Laotian President

en.body:
19 May 2014, Male'; President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has sent a message of sympathy ‎to President Choummaly Sayasone of Loas, following the passing away of ‎Defence Minister and senior officials of the Government, in a fatal plane ‎crash.‎

"It was with deep sadness that I learnt of the passing away of Defence ‎Minister Douangchay Phichit and senior officials of your Government, in a ‎fatal plane crash on 17th May 2014."‎

"At this time of grief, the Government and the people of the Maldives join me ‎in extending sincere condolences to you, the Government of Laos and the ‎friendly people."‎

"Please also convey our sincere condolences to the members of the bereaved ‎families."‎

ENDS.

en.body:
19 May 2014, Male'; The new Senegalese Ambassador accredited to the Maldives, Mr. ‎Amadou Mustapha Diouf, presented his letter of credence to President ‎Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom, this afternoon.‎

At the ceremony held at the President's Office to present the ‎credentials, President Yameen congratulated Ambassador Diouf on the ‎commencement of his term. Meeting the new Ambassador afterwards, the ‎President and the ‎Ambassador discussed bilateral relations that exist ‎between the two countries ‎and ways to further strengthen ties.‎

The President and the Ambassador further explored opportunities ‎‎for increasing cooperation between the Maldives and Senegal in the areas of ‎‎Tourism and Coastal Security.‎

‎ Continuing in this regard, Ambassador Amadou further reassured ‎President Yameen of Senegal's ‎continuous support and cooperation to the ‎Maldives.‎

The meeting was attended by Minister of Foreign Affairs, Hon. ‎Dunya Maumoon, and Minister at the President's Office, Hon. Abdulla ‎Ameen.‎
