en.title: The new Senegalese Ambassador calls on the Foreign Minister
en.description: 19 May 2014, Male'; The new Ambassador of the Republic of Senegal to the Maldives, His Excellency Mr. Amadou Mustapha Diouf, has called on the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon.
en.body:
19 May 2014, Male'; The new Ambassador of the Republic of Senegal to the Maldives, His Excellency Mr. Amadou Mustapha Diouf, has called on the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon.

At the meeting held this afternoon, Minister Dunya welcomed the Ambassador and congratulated him on his appointment. Minister also extended greetings and good wishes from the Government and the people of Maldives to the Government and the people of Republic of Senegal.

At the meeting, Minister Dunya remarked at the value attached by the Government of Maldives in respect of the bilateral ties that exist between the two countries, and highlighted the attributes of shared values, and mutual respect, that underlie the close relations.

Minister also expressed confidence that both Governments would engage in promoting economic cooperation in sectors such as security, fisheries development, tourism, transport, information technology, renewable energy and communication.

Minister Dunya was accompanied by Ms. Aishath Azeema, Joint Secretary of the Foreign Ministry of the Maldives.

ENDS.

en.title: President congratulates Indian Prime Minister Designate
en.description: 18 May 2014, Male'; During a telephone conversation today, President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has extended his congratulations to the Indian Prime Minister designate, Shri Narendra Modi, following the success in the recent Lok Sabha elections in India.
en.body:
18 May 2014, Male'; During a telephone conversation today, President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has extended his congratulations to the Indian Prime Minister designate, Shri Narendra Modi, following the success in the recent Lok Sabha elections in India.

Noting that BJP had secured a vast majority in the elections, the President said that the people's confidence in the party was evident in the election results.

Shri Narendra Modi highlighted the close bilateral relations between the Maldives and India, and spoke on the importance of further strengthening the relations.

Shri Narendra Modi expressed his gratitude to President Yameen for the good wishes. He assured the President that he would give high priority to build on the existing relations between the two countries, during his tenure as Prime Minister. Speaking in this regard, Shri Narendra Modi said that it was important for President Yameen and himself to meet and discuss further, on ways to develope the good relations between India and Maldives.

ENDS.

en.title: Foreign Minister Dunya attends the Top Achievers' Award Ceremony
en.description: 18 May 2014, Male'; Minister of Foreign Affairs, Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon has attended the Top Achiever's Award Ceremony held tonight at Dharubaaruge.
en.body:
18 May 2014, Male'; Minister of Foreign Affairs, Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon has attended the Top Achiever's Award Ceremony held tonight at Dharubaaruge.

A total of 479 students from all across the Maldives made it to the Top Ten Achievers List of 2013 Cambridge O'Level Examinations.

Amongst them, four students were classified as global top achievers and their awards were handed by the President, His Excellency Mr. Yameen Abdul Gayoom. Further, 21 students scoring top marks in different subjects, were classified between second and tenth places in the global top achievers list.

In addition, 40 students came in first place in the Top Ten achievers list, and eight students won the 'High Achiever' award.

Minister Dunya, was invited at the function to hand the awards to the group of students who won second place in the Top Ten achievers list.

Awards were also given to the schools with the best performance and results.

Compared to 2012 results, the number of students among the Top Ten list has increased by 53 students in 2013. Among the schools that took Cambridge examinations in 2013, a two-percent increase is noted amongst students who had passed in comparison to 2012 education ministry statistics.

ENDS.

en.title: Foreign Service Institute of Maldives (FOSIM) starts an Orientation Programme for the new staff
en.description: 18 May 2014, Male'; Foreign Service Institute of Maldives (FOSIM) has today started an Orientation Programme for the new staff who joined the Ministry from January 2013 to date.
en.body:
18 May 2014, Male'; Foreign Service Institute of Maldives (FOSIM) has today started an Orientation Programme for the new staff who joined the Ministry from January 2013 to date.

The Orientation Programme started this morning with opening remarks from the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon. In her remarks Minister stressed the importance of having regular orientation and refresher Programmes. Furthermore, each and every staff to be aware of the functions of the Ministry, Foreign Policy and the mandates of all the different sections of the Ministry. Minister also said that every single staff of the Ministry is responsible to represent the country and promote the best interests of the country according to the Foreign Policy.

The participants will be briefed on the Foreign Policy, Organization Structure and Departments of Ministry, Administration and Management, Civil Service Regulations and Guidelines, Human Rights, Anti-Corruption, Budgeting and Management, Protocol Theories and Practices, Drafting and Correspondence, Customer Care, Time Management, Etiquette and Ethics,

The objective of this Programme is to raise awareness about the Ministry and its functions, Foreign Policy, and to get new staff oriented to the daily work of the Ministry.

The Orientation Programme will be held from 18th to 26th May 2014.

ENDS.

en.title: Executive Director of ADB calls on the President
en.description: 18 May 2014, Male';Executive Director of the Asian Development Bank (ADB), Mr. Muhammad Sami Saeed has paid a courtesy call on President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom. The meeting was held this morning at the President's Office.
en.body:
18 May 2014, Male';Executive Director of the Asian Development Bank (ADB), Mr. Muhammad Sami Saeed has paid a courtesy call on President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom. The meeting was held this morning at the President's Office.

At the meeting, President Yameen noted that his administration was very ambitious in transforming the Maldives' economy, and said that the only way to achieve the Government's aspirations was through infrastructural development. In this regard, the President highlighted some of the mega projects planned for the future. The President briefed the ADB Executive Director on the areas the government accorded highest priority to, and reiterated the Government's commitment to improving the country's economy.

The Executive Director of ADB assured of the ADB's continuous support and assistance to the Maldives. He said that ADB would represent the Government's visions and aspirations on economic and infrastructural development. Mr. Muhammad Sami Saeed briefed the President on some projects currently undertaken by the ADB. He commended the Maldives on its developmental achievements. He said that he would put in every effort to strengthen the relationship between the Maldives and the organization, as the Maldives' representative on the Board of Directors of the ADB.

en.title: Foreign Minister Dunya sends a message of sympathy to Foreign Minister of Bangladesh
en.description: 18 May 2014, Male'; Minister of Foreign Affairs, Her Excellency Ms Dunya Maumoon has sent a message of sympathy to the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of Bangladesh , His Excellency Mr Abul Hassan Mahmood, following the tragic news of ferry incident in the Meghna River…
en.body:
18 May 2014, Male'; Minister of Foreign Affairs, Her Excellency Ms Dunya Maumoon has sent a message of sympathy to the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of Bangladesh , His Excellency Mr Abul Hassan Mahmood, following the tragic news of ferry incident in the Meghna River Thursday, 15th May 2014.

Minister Dunya's message reads as follows:

"It is with deep sorrow that I learnt of the news of the ferry incident on the Meghna River with the tragic death of over 50 people."

"On behalf of the Government and people of the Maldives, I wish to convey our deepest sympathies to the Government and people of Bangladesh and especially to the members of the bereaved families."

en.title: President sends congratulatory message to leader of India's Bharatiya Janata Party following election success
en.description: 16 May 2014, Male': President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has sent a congratulatory message to the leader of Bharatiya Janata Party, Shri Narendra Modi, following their victory in India's general elections.
en.body:
16 May 2014, Male': President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has sent a congratulatory message to the leader of Bharatiya Janata Party, Shri Narendra Modi, following their victory in India's general elections.

The President's message read as follows;

"On behalf of the Government and people of Maldives, I would like to congratulate you and the BJP-led alliance on the victory in the Lok Sabha elections."

"We are elated and have no doubt that India has chosen the most proficient leadership to enter a new era under BJP's leadership; and wish you and the citizens of India every success and prosperity."

"The Maldives attaches the highest importance to its relations with India. As close neighbours with a unique relationship and deep links across all walks of life, our relations are closely intertwined. I therefore remain confident that cooperation between the Maldives and India will further develop under your leadership and guidance in a constructive manner. We look forward to working with you and your colleagues to further enhance our cooperation for the benefit of the people of both our countries."

"Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration."

ENDS.

en.title: "The Bill on Sexual Abuse and Harrassment and the Bill on Sexual Offences are landmark laws in the fight towards eliminating gender based violence" Minister Dunya
en.description: 15 May 2014, Male'; The Bill on Sexual Abuse and Harrassment and the Bill on Sexual Offences are landmark laws in the fight towards eliminating gender based violence" said Her Excellency Ms Dunya Maumoon, Minister of Foreign Affairs. President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom ratified the two bills on…
en.body:
15 May 2014, Male'; The Bill on Sexual Abuse and Harrassment and the Bill on Sexual Offences are landmark laws in the fight towards eliminating gender based violence" said Her Excellency Ms Dunya Maumoon, Minister of Foreign Affairs. President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom ratified the two bills on 13 May 2014. They were passed by the Parliament at the Eight Sitting of its First Session on 27 April 2014.

Welcoming the ratification of the two bills, Minister Dunya noted that the Maldives has been working to improve the legislative framework on gender based violence and gender discrimination, while working to adopt the norms and traditions associated with gender equality. In this regard, she reiterated the Government's efforts to formulate and pass the two bills on sexual harassment and sexual offences, as well as in promoting the rights enshrined in the Convention on Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, and gender mainstreaming in the Maldives.

Noting the numerous incidences of violence against women around the world, Minister Dunya particularly noted the recent abducting of more than 200 school girls by Boko Haram in Nigeria. "Such incidents against young girls should not happen anywhere in the world. Children must be protected, and their right to an education, to a safe life, must be guaranteed regardless of gender", said Minister Dunya, while also condemning acts of violence against young girls and women in Maldives.

The Minister once again highlighted the Government's and her own commitment to eradicating gender based violence and to gender equality in the Maldives and around the world.

ENDS

en.title: President sends message of sympathy to the President of Turkey
en.description: 15 May 2014, Male';President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has sent a message of sympathy ‎to President Abdullah Gul, following the deadly explosion at a coal mine in ‎Soma.‎
en.body:
15 May 2014, Male';President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has sent a message of sympathy ‎to President Abdullah Gul, following the deadly explosion at a coal mine in ‎Soma.‎

The President's message read as follows;‎

"I was deeply shocked to learn about the deadly explosion at a coal mine in ‎Soma, causing the loss of many innocent lives and injury to thousands of ‎people. While the search for survivors continues, we pray that, of those that ‎remain unaccounted for so far, more victims can be saved."‎

"At this time of national tragedy, the Government and the people of the ‎Maldives join me in sending our profound sympathy to you, the Government ‎and the people of Turkey. I wish the recovery efforts every success and ‎commend the tenacity of the Turkish people in the face of such tragedy."‎

"Please also convey our sincere condolences to the members of the bereaved ‎families."‎

en.title: The Government's highest priority is women's empowerment - President Yameen
en.description: 15 May 2014, Male';President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has said that the Government's highest priority was to give real empowerment for women, and to empower women economically and financially. The President made this remark while speaking at the official function held this morning to mark this…
en.body:
15 May 2014, Male';President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has said that the Government's highest priority was to give real empowerment for women, and to empower women economically and financially. The President made this remark while speaking at the official function held this morning to mark this year's International Women's Day.

In his speech, the President noted that a high number of Maldivian women in the island communities were working in the agricultural and fisheries sectors. And that the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) allocates 60% of its loans especially to women, in order to facilitate more opportunities for women in the fisheries and agriculture industries. Similarly, the President said that 60% of loan allocation for innovation in the fisheries sector was also made especially for women.

Speaking at the function, the President said that the most vital instrument in empowering women was educating them, and highlighted the importance of it. Speaking in this regard, the President said that the Government's policy was to provide education to all children and not exclude any one.

In his speech, the President underlined the continuous efforts being made globally in advocating for women's rights. In this regard, the President pointed out that it is being called for internationally, not to deprive women of their rights, to provide equal educational opportunities for girls, and to let women's voices be heard in the lawmaking process.

At the function held today, the President conferred the Rehendi Award, introduced this year to recognize outstanding service of women to national development and the society, to Juwairiya Wajdee and Aminath Nasheeda, both renowned local chefs.

First Lady Madam Fathimath Ibrahim presented the commemorative brooches to the recipients, and Minister of Health and Gender, Dr Maryam Shakeela gave away the prize offered by the Bank of Maldives.

During the meeting which was held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs this morning, Minister Dunya welcomed the Regional Director to the Maldives, and extended gratitude to the contribution that UNFPA has made to the Maldivian society and the development and progress of the country.

During the meeting, the Minister and the Regional Director discussed opportunities and avenues for further expanding UNFPA's role in the Maldives, especially with regard to women, girls, and young people.

en.title: “Investing in the youth is investing in the future” says Minister Dunya
en.description: 13 May 2014, Male’; Minister of Foreign Affairs , Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon made these remarks, attending as Chief Guest, to inaugurate the Regional Consultative Meeting to Finalize the SAARCYouth Charter and Action Plan, held todayat the Traders Hotel.
en.body:
13 May 2014, Male’; Minister of Foreign Affairs , Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon made these remarks, attending as Chief Guest, to inaugurate the Regional Consultative Meeting to Finalize the SAARCYouth Charter and Action Plan, held todayat the Traders Hotel.

The SAARC’s Regional Consultative Session, which forms part of the three day event hosted by the Government of Maldives, in collaboration with UNFPA to finalize the SAARCYouth Charter and Action Plan for 2014 to 2017, is to take place from 13th to 14th of May 2014. A preceding youth workshop was also held yesterday, to obtain views from the youth themselves, on the Youth Charter and Action Plan.

Minister Dunya, emphasizing the role of youthas leaders and decision makers of tomorrow, stated in her speech;

“Investing in the youth is investing in the future. They are the leaders and decision makers of tomorrow. They are the ones to shape the destiny of our region and the world in the coming years. We cannot deny them their rights, opportunities or the resources that will enable them to play this important role. We need to ensure their active participation and ensure that their voices are heard.”

Minister Dunya also underscored the importance making youth policies a priority. In this regard, she stated:

“We must eradicate violence and abuse of young people, especially girls and other marginalized groups. We must not let youth be deprived from an education or access to decent work. We must invest in the health and well-being of the youth.”

The SAARC’s Youth Charter, once finalized, will provide a collaborative framework for its member states to pool their resources towards enriching health, well-being and potential of youth across region. The Charter, focuses on 5 key areas of action, namely, Enabling Environment, Gender Equality, Education and Skills Development, Employment and Health. The Charter envisions the formulation of new youth-centric policies and re-focusing of youth priorities at the national and regional level. In this regard, the objective of the Consultative Session is to validate the SAARC Youth Charter and set in motion the SAARC Youth Action Plan for 2014 to 2017.

ENDS.

en.title: Address by H.E. Ms. Dunya Maumoon, Minister of Foreign Affairs and Chairman of SAARC Council of Ministers, at the Opening Ceremony of the Regional Consultative Meeting to finalize SAARC Youth Charter and Action Plan, 12 - 14 May 2014, Male', Maldives
en.description: Honourable Ministers, Distinguished Delegates, Ladies and Gentlemen,
en.body:
Honourable Ministers, Distinguished Delegates, Ladies and Gentlemen,

Assalaamu alaikum and a very good morning.

On behalf of the Government of Maldives, it gives me great pleasure to extend a very warm welcome to the distinguished delegates and youth representatives, to the Maldives,. I believe the outcome of this meeting will pave the way for far-reaching positive impacts on the lives of young people in the South Asia region, who will carry this region forward, tomorrow

The youth of today represent the biggest generation of youth in human history. There are, at present, over 1.2 billion youth globally. 62% of them live in Asia and 26% live in the SAARC region alone. The regions is currently in a critical demographic period where the number of work-age adults exceeds the children and the elderly. This increased proportion of youth in the total population provides a demographic bonus,this is an excellent opportunity for accelerated and robust development. the benefits of this critical period can only be achieved if the youth are empowered with the education, skills, and opportunities to positively contribute to the advancement of themselves and their societies.

The reasons for placing youth at the very centre of the development agenda is compelling. We must ensure their meaningful participation in the development process. We must promote the health, well-being and potential rights of all young people and most importantly, we must include them in the design and implementation of policies and programs, especially those that affect their lives. In fact youth have to own these policies and programmes and be the agents of change.The vision of President Yameen Abdul Gayoom is encapsulated in the slogan "Youth, Economy, Hope" which cleary spells our the focus of our government on empowering youth.

Distinguished Delegates,

Ever since its inception, SAARC has continued to attach due priority to the issues related to youth. The Ministerial Conference on Youth in South Asia held in May 1994 focused on the broad theme youth and development.. In fact, the Year 1994 was designated as the "SAARC Year of Youth". Then in 1995, the SAARC Youth Resolution was adopted to advance the overall development of youth in the region.

SAARC youth camps are being held periodically on a designated theme with a view to promote cultural interaction among the youth, with the most recent being the Fourth SAARC Youth Camp hosted by India in February 2013 on the theme "Youth as Ambassadors in Global partnership for Development".

The SAARC Youth Awards Scheme was instituted in 1996 to provide recognition to extraordinary young talents and encourage the overall development of the youth in the region. Since then, eleven SAARC youth awards have been given to deserving young people from different Member States. I am very pleased to inform that the SAARC Youth Award 2011 on the theme "Youth Leadership in the Fight Against Social Ills" was awarded to a young man from the Maldives, Mr. Mohamed Faseen Rafiu.

Distinguished Delegates,

Today, as we move towards finalizing the SAARC Youth Charter, I believe that this Charter and its Action Plan will be an exemplary regional framework where the true aspirations, hopes and dreams of the South Asian youth themselves are reflected. I am pleased that fruitful discussions were held during the Youth Workshop yesterday. The energy, enthusiasm and fresh ideas of our youth, will surely provide the right inspiration and impetus for the delegations as they begin the government consultations shortly.

I believe that this Youth Charter, with its five key areas of focus, Enabling Environment, Gender Equality, Education and Skills Development, Employment and Health, provides a sound foundation for the South Asian nations where efforts of Member States will complement each other in promoting the health, well-being and potential rights of all young people, male and female

Distinguished Delegates,

The estimated population of Maldives currently stands at 350,000. Of this, over 50% comprise people under the age of 25 years and the largest cohort, about 25% of the population is between 15 to 25 years. The rapid changes in our traditional lifestyles, attitudes and values have enormous implications and potential, especially for this young population.Their lives are subject to currents and forces very different from those experienced by their parents. While they are faced with numerous opportunities and access, the risks and dangers that can threaten their well-being has increased.

The Government of Maldives, recognizes the importance of empowering youth and officially started the development of youth activities here in the Maldives, in August 1980, with the establishment of the Youth Council by the then President Maumoon Abdul Gayoom. This was a very productive beginning for youth-centered development programs

Since then,we have made significant achievements. A comprehensive National Youth Policy was launched in 2003, which addressed key areas of education, employment, urban and rural disparities, housing, family, health, environment, crime and delinquency and youth participation. Today, a legislative framework, "Maldives Youth Bill" has been drafted and is in the process of being finalized. However, against these achievements, challenges faced by the youth in the Maldives and youth living elsewhere in the world have increased manifold.

Distinguished Delegates,

Investing in the youth is investing in the future. They are the leaders and decision makers of tomorrow.They are the ones to shape the destiny of our region and the world in the coming years. We cannot deny them their rights, opportunities or the resources that will enable them to play this important role. We need to ensure their active participation and ensure that their voices are heard.

We must make youth policies a priority. We must protect the rights of youth through legislative and administrative measures. We must eliminate discrimination against the youth based on gender, race, religion, caste, class or disability. We must eradicate violence and abuse of young people, especially girls and other marginalized groups.We must not let youth be deprived from an education or access to decent work. We must invest in the health and well-being of the youth.

Tomorrow, as the SAARC Youth Charter is finalized, let that be a significant moment in the history of South Asia, where we pledge to do all we can and play our part in the making of history by our young people. Let us pledge to invest in the future of South Asia.

Thank You.

ENDS.

en.title: "People living with Thalassemia should be accorded equal rights in society" says Minister Dunya Maumoon
en.description: 8 May 2014:"People living with Thalassemia should be accorded equal rights and equal treatment" says Her Excellency Ms Dunya Maumoon, Minister of Foreign Affairs. On the occasion of World Thalassemia Day, Minister Dunya urged all stakeholders to ensure that the rights accorded to people living with…
en.body:
8 May 2014:"People living with Thalassemia should be accorded equal rights and equal treatment" says Her Excellency Ms Dunya Maumoon, Minister of Foreign Affairs. On the occasion of World Thalassemia Day, Minister Dunya urged all stakeholders to ensure that the rights accorded to people living with Thalassemia are provided fully.

Reflecting on the theme for the year "Economic Recession: Observe-Join-Safeguard Health", Minister Dunya urged that the responsibilities towards all people living with Thalassemia, especially children, should not be sacrificed in light of austerity, or financial cut-backs. These rights include those guaranteed by the Constitution of the Maldives, and especially in the Thalassemia Act ratified on 10 May 2012. She also urged civil society and the private sector to contribute to the efforts to realise the needs of these valuable members of the society.

In her message, Minister Dunya stated that "the President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom's Government is committed to work closely and firmly with the people of the Maldives, both at domestic and international stage to address the problems faced by thalassemia patients."

There are currently 588 patients registered and receiving treatment for Thalassemia in the Maldives. World Thalassemia Day is celebrated on 8 May, on the initiative of the World Health Organisation, in order to raise public awareness about the disease, prevention measures and measures to avoid its transmission.

ENDS

en.title: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the UNissues a joint statment on the closure of UN Building.
en.description: 05 May 2014, Male'; Ministry of Foriegn Affairs and the United Nations in Maldives has issued a joint statement regarding the closure of UN Building. The joint statment reads as follows;
en.body:
05 May 2014, Male'; Ministry of Foriegn Affairs and the United Nations in Maldives has issued a joint statement regarding the closure of UN Building. The joint statment reads as follows;

"The UN Building on Buruzu Magu was vacated on 30 April 2014 due to structural damage to the building and concerns for the security and safety of the staff working in the building.The UN agencies resident in the UN Building are now operating from different locations in Male' under interim arrangements until semi-permanent offices are secured. Staff from some agencies have also been co-located to Government offices, providing for the continuation of important programmatic activities.

The decision to vacate the Building was made by the UN after it was found that the Building is structurally unsafe for use. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the UN have been holding extensive discussions over the past one year on issues related to the condition of the UN Building and in finding a longer-term solution forsuitable office space for the UN in the Maldives."

en.title: Foreign Minister Dunya sends message of condolence to the Foreign Minister of Afghanistan
en.description: 04 May 2014, Male'; Minister of Foreign Affairs, Her Excellency Ms Dunya Maumoon has sent a message of condolence to the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan His Excellency Mr. Zarar Ahmad Osmani, following the deadly mudslide in the north-east province of Badakhshan…
en.body:
04 May 2014, Male'; Minister of Foreign Affairs, Her Excellency Ms Dunya Maumoon has sent a message of condolence to the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan His Excellency Mr. Zarar Ahmad Osmani, following the deadly mudslide in the north-east province of Badakhshan on Friday, 02 May 2014.

Minister Dunya's message reads as follows:

"It is with deep sorrow that I learnt of the tragic news of the landslide that killed over 2000 people and left several unaccounted for and many more homeless since last Friday.

As the country mourns this great tragedy, I wish to convey personal condolences to your Excellency and the people of Afghanistan especially to those who have lost their loved ones. My thoughts and prayers are with the bereaved families and pray to Almighty Allah to grant them the strength and fortitude to bear this loss."

ENDS.

en.title: President sends message of sympathy to the President of Afghanistan
en.description: 04 May 2014, Male'; President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has sent a message of sympathy ‎to President Hamid Karzai of Afghanistan, following the deadly mudslide in ‎the north-east province of Badakhshan.‎
en.body:
04 May 2014, Male'; President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has sent a message of sympathy ‎to President Hamid Karzai of Afghanistan, following the deadly mudslide in ‎the north-east province of Badakhshan.‎

The President's message read as follows;‎

"I was deeply saddened to learn about the deadly mudslide in the north-east ‎province of Badakhshan, causing the loss of many innocent lives, injury to ‎thousands of people, as well as irrevocable damage to property and ‎infrastructure. While the search for survivors continues, we pray that, of ‎those that remain unaccounted for so far, more victims can be saved."‎

"At this time of tragedy, the Government and the people of the Maldives join ‎me in sending our profound sympathy to you, the Government and the ‎brotherly people of Afghanistan. I wish the recovery efforts every success and ‎commend the tenacity of the Afghan people in the face of such tragedy."‎

"Please also convey our sincere condolences to the members of the bereaved ‎families, and our solidarity with the grieving residents of Badakhshan and the ‎rescue workers."‎

ENDS.

29 April 2014, Male'; Ambassador of the United States to the Maldives Michele J. Sison ‎has paid a courtesy call on President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom. The ‎meeting was held this morning at the President's Office.‎

Discussions at the meeting were focused on the bilateral relations ‎‎between the Maldives and the United States, and on ways to further ‎‎enhance cooperation between both countries.‎

Noting that economic transformation was on top of his ‎Government's ‎agenda, President Yameen shared with Ambassador Sison ‎the Government strategies to improve the country's current economic ‎situation.‎

Ambassador Sison briefed the President on the ongoing and ‎planned US aided developmental programmes in the Maldives. Further, the ‎Ambassador reassured of US's continuous support and cooperation to the ‎Maldives.‎

President Yameen was joined at the call by Minister of Foreign ‎Affairs, Hon. Dunya Maumoon, Minister at the President's Office, Hon. ‎Mohamed Hussain Shareef and the Additional Secretary at the Ministry of ‎Foreign Affairs, Mr. Ali Naseer Mohamed.‎

en.title: "The future of Commonwealth lies in the celebration of diversity" Former President Maumoon Abdul Gayoom
en.description: 27 April 2014;Former President of the Maldives, His Excellency Maumoon Abdul Gayoom has said that the future of the Commonwealth lies in the celebration of the diversity that exists within the organisation.
en.body:
27 April 2014;Former President of the Maldives, His Excellency Maumoon Abdul Gayoom has said that the future of the Commonwealth lies in the celebration of the diversity that exists within the organisation.

President Gayoom was the Chief Guest, at a special event held in Colombo last night by the Commonwealth Chair-in-Office and President of Sri Lanka Mr. Mahinda Rajapaksa to celebrate the cultural diversity of the Commonwealth.

The Commonwealth is an organization of 53 member states spanning all the continents, and encompasses all the major languages, religions and political ideologies of the world. The Maldives joined the Commonwealth under President Gayoom's leadership in 1982.

In his speech, President Gayoom said that the diversity within the Commonwealth makes the organisation one of the strongest international bodies in the world today. The former President, also highlighted the importance of mutual respect, tolerance, and understanding between the countries of the Commonwealth, in order to foster peace and create an environment conducive for development to happen. The Commonwealth brings together, to the same table, countries of different cultures, development levels and political ideologies, as equals. This, President Gayoom, said, must be celebrated and respected.

ENDS

en.title: "The diversity of the Commonwealth has made us stronger" President Yameen Abdul Gayoom
en.description: 27 April 2014;His Excellency Mr Yameen Abdul Gayoom, President of the Republic of Maldives has said that it is the diversity of the Commonwealth that has made it stronger.
en.body:
27 April 2014;His Excellency Mr Yameen Abdul Gayoom, President of the Republic of Maldives has said that it is the diversity of the Commonwealth that has made it stronger.

President Yameen made the statement in a message sent to the Commonwealth Chair-in-Office and President of Sri Lanka Mr. Mahinda Rajapaksa, for a special event held last night in Colombo to celebrate the cultural diversity of the Commonwealth.

The President expressed his hope that the common beliefs shared by the Commonwealth countries will guide us towards finding mutually beneficial solutions to the global problems facing the world today.

The President further conveyed his appreciation to the Sri Lankan Government, for hosting a special event in its capacity as Chair-in-Office of the Commonwealth to celebrate the cultural diversity of the organization, in which former President of Maldives, His Excellency Maumoon Abdul Gayoom participated as the Chief Guest.

ENDS

en.title: Foreign Minister Dunya concludes Official Visit to Sri Lanka
en.description: 28 April 2014, Male'; Minister of Foreign Affairs, Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon has arrived this evening, on conclusion of her official visit to Sri Lanka.
en.body:
28 April 2014, Male'; Minister of Foreign Affairs, Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon has arrived this evening, on conclusion of her official visit to Sri Lanka.

Minister Dunya held official meetings with the Sri Lanka leadership and discussed follow up matters that were discussed during the visit of His Excellency President Yameen's State visit to Sri Lanka in January.

Minister Dunya reiterated President Yameen's invitation to President Rajapaksa. Minister also discussed allocation of land by both countries for the construction of High Commission buildings and discussed ongoing collaboration in education and health sectors. President Rajapaksa assured the support of the Government of Sri Lanka for the development initiative of the Government of Maldives.

Minister Dunya's visit to Sri Lanka was on the invitation of Minister of External Affairs of Sri Lanka H. E. Prof. G.L. Peiris, to attend an event hosted by H.E. President Mahinda Rajapaksa in his capacity as Chair-in-Office of the Commonwealth to celebrate the Cultural Diversity of the Commonwealth.

ENDS.

en.body:
26 April 2014, Male'; President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has said that the Maldives Investment Forum held in Singapore on Friday, 25th April 2014, was a very successful event that caught the interest of many foreign investors. The President made this remark while speaking to the local media this evening, on arrival from Singapore.

The President noted that promoting the economic sectors of the country must be an ongoing process. In this regard, the President highlighted the promotional work being undertaken by the Government, to reintroduce the Maldives' economy to the world, and to promote its numerous economic sectors.

ENDS.
